title: Teriyaki Salmon
subtitle: Pan-fried salmon glazed with soy, mirin, and honey
excerpt: Salmon fillets marinated in a classic teriyaki glaze and cooked in a hot pan until the sauce becomes thick and lacquered. Ready in under 20 minutes once the marinade time is done.
sourceNotes: Standard Japanese teriyaki preparation applied to salmon. Sake, mirin, soy sauce, and honey are the canonical four teriyaki components.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate for up to 24 hours in the fridge.

content.text: Do not move the salmon while it is searing. Let the skin crisp up fully on one side before turning.

items.prepNote: 4 pieces of about 150g each, skin on

content.text: Mix the soy sauce, mirin, sake, honey, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil in a shallow dish.
Add the salmon fillets skin-side up. Cover and chill for 30 minutes.
Remove the salmon from the marinade and set the marinade aside.
Heat a frying pan over medium-high heat. Add a small drizzle of oil. Place the salmon skin-side down. Cook for 4 minutes without moving it.
Flip the salmon. Pour the reserved marinade into the pan around the fish. Cook for 3 more minutes until the sauce reduces and becomes sticky.
Spoon the sauce over the salmon and serve immediately with steamed rice.

items.symptom: Glaze burnt in the pan before salmon cooked through.
items.cause: Heat was too high when the marinade was added.
items.fix: Reduce heat to medium when adding marinade; swirl to prevent burning.

items.symptom: Skin stuck to the pan when flipping.
items.cause: Skin not fully released; it needed more time on the first side.
items.fix: If the salmon resists the spatula, give it another minute.

items.symptom: Sauce did not thicken and glaze.
items.cause: Too much liquid in the pan or heat too low.
items.fix: Raise heat and simmer the sauce briefly before spooning over.
